name: Business
context_hint: Your job and its hours, current priorities and deadlines, meetings pattern, what you're building on the side.
goal: A healthy working week: a protected focus block, a regular marketing slot and a full-time job that ends on time.

sources.mark2008: Mark G, Gudith D, Klocke U. The cost of interrupted work: more speed and stress. Proc CHI, 2008.
sources.ericsson1993: Ericsson KA, Krampe RT, Tesch-Römer C. The role of deliberate practice in the acquisition of expert performance. Psychol Rev, 1993.
sources.lally2010: Lally P, van Jaarsveld CHM, Potts HWW, Wardle J. How are habits formed: modelling habit formation in the real world. Eur J Soc Psychol, 2010.
sources.kecklund2016: Kecklund G, Axelsson J. Health consequences of shift work and insufficient sleep. BMJ, 2016.
sources.albulescu2022: Albulescu P, Macsinga I, Rusu A, Sulea C, Bodnaru A, Tulbure BT. 'Give me a break!' A systematic review and meta-analysis on the efficacy of micro-breaks for increasing well-being and performance. PLoS One, 2022.
sources.kivimaki2015: Kivimäki M et al. Long working hours and risk of coronary heart disease and stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis of published and unpublished data for 603 838 individuals. Lancet, 2015.
sources.sonnentag2015: Sonnentag S, Fritz C. Recovery from job stress: the stressor-detachment model as an integrative framework. J Organ Behav, 2015.

phases.goal: Focused work first, outward work after lunch

rules.title: Focused development block
rules.weekly_why: Five protected focus blocks a week carry most of the week's real progress.
rules.label: Development
rules.why: Interruptions raise stress and time pressure; experts do their hardest practice in limited, protected morning sessions.
rules.advice: Two hours of development with notifications off.

nudge.text: Focused block starts in 5 minutes: development. Notifications off.

rules.title: Marketing slot
rules.weekly_why: Marketing compounds when it is frequent: at least four slots a week.
rules.label: Marketing
rules.why: Doing the same task in the same slot every day makes it automatic faster than doing it whenever there is time.
rules.advice: One hour of marketing after lunch.

rules.title: Start work at the usual time
rules.label: Start work
rules.weekly_why: Four regular starts out of five keep the working day anchored.
rules.why: A fixed start anchors the working day and protects the evening; irregular working hours are linked with shorter sleep and worse health.

rules.title: Break away from the screen
rules.label: Afternoon break
rules.weekly_why: A real break on most workdays.
rules.why: Short breaks during work raise vigour and reduce fatigue (meta-analysis of micro-break studies).
rules.advice: 10 minutes away from the screen — walk, stretch or step outside.

nudge.text: Take 10 minutes away from the screen — it pays back in focus.

rules.title: Finish work on time
rules.label: Finish on time
rules.weekly_why: Long hours are the risk: finish on time on at least four days.
rules.why: Regularly working long hours (55+ a week) is linked to a higher risk of stroke and coronary heart disease than standard hours.
rules.advice: Wrap up and log off at your usual time.

nudge.text: 15 minutes to the end of your working day — start wrapping up.

rules.title: Switch off after work
rules.label: Switch off after work
rules.weekly_why: Most evenings free of work messages.
rules.why: Mentally detaching from work in the evening is central to recovery; staying connected predicts exhaustion the next day.
rules.advice: No work email or messages tonight.

nudge.text: Work's done — notifications off for the evening.
